findings.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from the start of BuildIndex (it now only guards the final cache write) allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource to both execute bleve.New(dir) on the same file path, and bleve.New returns an error when the path already exists. Because the cache entry is only published after the full build completes (b.cache[key] = idx at line ~137), two concurrent callers for the same uncached/evicted key (e.g., a user-triggered Search racing a watch-driven handleEvent build) both enter the file-backed branch; the loser fails with bleve's 'path already exists' error and the search-index build for that tenant fails, where the previous coarse lock serialized creation and made this impossible.

[ADVISORY] The new log line 'search index initialized' with duration_secs and total_docs executes immediately after the background build goroutine is spawned (the `}()` above it), so it reports initialization as complete with a duration near zero and a TotalDocs() count sampled before the index has been built. Operators and dashboards/alerts keyed on this log line or on IndexCreationTime-style signals will conclude the search index is ready when the actual document build is still running in the goroutine, and total_docs will read 0 or a partial count until the async build finishes.

[ADVISORY] The new unconditional postgres skip removes all Drone CI coverage for this instrumentation-server integration test against postgres, and since the PR simultaneously rewrites server initialization (Init moved to NewResourceServer, per-method Init calls deleted), the skip may be masking a failure this very diff introduced. Any postgres-specific regression in the server construction/initialization path changed by this PR (eager Init, watcher/search reorder) will no longer be caught in CI; the 'Works locally' comment indicates the failure is environment/ordering dependent, i.e., exactly the class of regression CI exists to catch, and the TODO skip gives no path to re-enabling it.

[BUG] The diff skips TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer for postgres in the same PR that changes server initialization timing, dropping the only CI verification of the server startup path for postgres and likely suppressing a failure caused by this very diff (eager s.Init at construction now runs the full search index build inside NewResourceServer, which the skipped integration test exercises). A regression in server startup/index-build behavior (including one introduced by this diff's move of Init from lazy per-request to construction time) ships undetected for postgres; the 'Works locally' note suggests an environment/timing-dependent failure consistent with the new blocking init, and skipping removes the signal instead of resolving it.

[BUG] The reorder of Init (search.init now runs before initWatcher) and the removal of all lazy per-method Init calls are behavior-bearing changes with zero test coverage in this diff — the only test file touched (pkg/server/module_server_test.go) adds only a skip, and no test asserts either that resources written while the index builds are still indexed or that NewResourceServer fails fast on init error. A regression in the init ordering (e.g., events silently dropped or the watcher never started after a partial init failure) or in the fail-fast construction contract passes CI unnoticed and surfaces as an empty/stale search index or a broken storage server in production.

[ADVISORY] Moving search.init ahead of initWatcher opens a gap in which every write that lands between the index snapshot taken by search.init (which the new log line at search.go:216 shows can take a long time, logging duration_secs) and the start of the watch loop is never delivered to handleEvent, leaving those resources absent from search results until the next full rebuild. Users who create or update dashboards/folders during a slow index build (startup or tenant onboarding with large namespaces) get no search hits for those resources until a subsequent full reindex, with no error or log indicating the gap.

[ADVISORY] Narrowing cacheMu to only the final cache write (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137-139) removes the serialization of concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key, so two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource both proceed: on the file-backed path the second bleve.New(dir) at line 99 fails because the index directory already exists, returning an error for a routine concurrent rebuild, and on the mem-only path both indexes are built with the loser leaking its in-memory index. Under concurrent first-access or overlapping rebuild triggers for the same namespace/resource, callers receive spurious 'index already exists'-class errors from BuildIndex, or duplicate memory-only indexes are constructed and discarded; this changed concurrency behavior is also unverified — no test in the diff exercises concurrent BuildIndex.

[ADVISORY] NewResourceServer now returns a hard construction error when s.Init fails, but Init also logs 'error initializing resource server' internally (line ~309), so an init failure at startup is double-logged and, more importantly, any deployment path that previously tolerated a failed lazy init and served Read/List after retrying now cannot start at all — a silent change to the public construction contract with no migration note or fallback path in the diff. Operators upgrading Grafana on a tenant whose index build fails at startup (e.g., disk or permissions issue on the bleve root directory) get a total storage-server startup failure where the previous lazy-init behavior allowed the process to start and retry per request; the behavior change is untested and undocumented in this diff.

[BUG] Removing the cacheMu hold for the duration of BuildIndex turns the check-then-build sequence into a race: two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource can both miss the cache and both call bleve.New(dir, ...) on the same directory, where the second bleve.New fails because the index already exists (and for mem-only indexes both build duplicate indexes). Two concurrent first-time searches/builds for the same namespace+resource race; one caller gets a spurious build error (or duplicated work/memory) where the old global mutex guaranteed exactly one build and a cached result. The mutex now only protects the final map insert, so the expensive create path it used to serialize is unserialized with no per-key guard introduced.

[BUG] Reordering Init so search.init runs before initWatcher opens a window where writes committed after the index build snapshot but before the watcher starts are neither in the index nor observed by any watcher, leaving the search index permanently stale until a full rebuild. Previously the watcher was started before search.init, so events written during the (possibly long) index build were received and applied; after this reorder any write landing in the build-to-watch-start gap is silently missing from search results with no event to correct it. This behavioral reordering is not required by the performance goal and is not traceable to a stated requirement.

[BUG] The new postgres skip ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.') disables CI coverage for the server-startup integration test in the same PR that moves initialization into NewResourceServer, masking a failure this change most likely introduced rather than fixing it. The only integration test in the diff exercising server startup no longer runs against postgres in CI, so a real regression in constructor-time Init (e.g. ctx cancellation or DB-readiness assumptions from calling s.Init(ctx) inside NewResourceServer) ships undetected; developers trusting 'Works locally' lose the safety net exactly on the behavior this PR changed.

[ADVISORY] Calling s.Init(ctx) inside NewResourceServer converts a per-request lazy failure into a hard construction-time failure: with search configured, startup now blocks on a full index build and any Init error (or caller ctx timeout) prevents the server from being created at all. Operators with large indexes get long blocking startup, and any transient DB error at boot now fails server construction where previously the server came up and requests surfaced Init errors lazily; there is no feature flag or options entry to retain the old lazy behavior, so this cannot be disabled without a code deploy. The change is a behavior/deployment-semantics change riding in a 'performance optimizations' PR without a stated requirement.

[ADVISORY] The new 'search index initialized' log line reports duration in whole seconds via time.Now().Unix() subtraction, so any build under one second logs duration_secs=0 and multi-minute builds are also truncated, making the metric misleading for the performance work it was added to support. Anyone using this log line (added specifically in this PR as observability for index-build performance) cannot distinguish sub-second builds from near-zero or compare builds finer than 1s; time.Since(start) or the existing histogram metric would report the real value.

[BUG] Reordering init() before initWatcher() in server.Init opens a lost-events window: the search index is built from a snapshot, and every resource written between that snapshot read and the watcher subscribing afterwards is never indexed, because the previous watcher-first order was what guaranteed those in-flight writes were captured and replayed into the freshly built index. For the duration of the (potentially minutes-long) index build, any create/update/delete committed to the store is silently absent from search results indefinitely — not just during the build — since nothing re-syncs the index afterward; users see stale or missing dashboards/folders in search until a full re-index is triggered.

[BUG] Removing the whole-body cacheMu lock from BuildIndex turns the cache insert into an unguarded check-then-insert: two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key both pass the cache check and both execute bleve.New on the same on-disk directory path (size > FileThreshold), where bleve.New fails when the path already exists, or both create duplicate mem-only indexes with last-writer-wins on b.cache. Previously the second caller blocked on cacheMu and received the first caller's fully built index; now one of the two concurrent builders gets an unexpected 'index already exists' error for file-backed namespaces (a failed search-index build that used to be impossible), or an orphaned duplicate in-memory index leaks for memory-backed ones.

[ADVISORY] NewResourceServer now runs the full Init — including the potentially long-running search index build — synchronously under the constructor's context, converting what was a per-request lazy-init failure into a hard startup failure and binding init lifetime to whatever context the caller happened to pass to construction. For large deployments the initial index build blocks process startup with no bound visible in this diff, and if the construction context is cancelled or carries a timeout, server creation fails outright where previously the system could start and serve non-search traffic; rolling deploys also see delayed readiness proportional to index size.

[ADVISORY] The reorder changes failure blast radius: because search.init now runs before initWatcher and both are gated on s.initErr == nil, a search-backend-only failure (index build error) now leaves initErr set and skips initWatcher, disabling the watch/update propagation pipeline entirely even though it is independent of search. An outage or misconfiguration of the search backend now degrades the whole resource server's change-propagation (watchers get nothing), where previously a search failure could not prevent the watcher from starting; operators debugging 'clients stop receiving watch events' must trace it back to a search index error.

[BUG] NewResourceServer now runs s.Init(ctx) eagerly at construction under the constructor's context, converting a first-request lazy init into a hard startup dependency. A transient DB failure (or a cancelled/short-lived constructor ctx) during boot now prevents the server from being constructed at all, where previously the process came up and the first request bore/reported the init error; additionally, the full search index build (which search.go's own comment says 'will block startup and continued execution') now runs synchronously inside NewResourceServer, so large deployments block process startup for the entire index rebuild instead of serving degraded until first request. This is a deployment/lifecycle semantics change, not a performance optimization, and nothing in the PR records that the objective was expanded to include changing startup behavior.

[ADVISORY] Twelve exported RPC methods (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob) silently lose their self-initializing contract: the `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { return nil, err }` guard is stripped from each without any change to their documented behavior. Any caller that constructs a server struct outside NewResourceServer (tests, alternative builders, out-of-tree integrations) and relied on 'call any method and the server initializes itself' now executes against uninitialized backends — e.g. Read/List hit a nil store, Search returns 'search index not configured' — instead of getting the previous init-or-error behavior. The public contract changed with no signature change and no explicit acceptance that the lazy-init guarantee was being removed.

[BUG] Init silently reorders search.init to run before initWatcher, so there is now a window after the index snapshot is built during which the watcher is not running and incoming writes are not observed. A write that lands between the completion of search.init's full index build and initWatcher starting is never delivered to handleEvent; that resource remains absent/stale in search results until some later write to the same resource happens — for a quiescent resource, indefinitely. Under the previous ordering (watcher first, then index build) a write during the build triggered getOrCreateIndex/build and was folded in, so this stale-index window is a new failure mode introduced by an unexplained reorder inside a PR titled 'Performance Optimizations'.

[BUG] Removing the function-wide cacheMu lock from BuildIndex allows concurrent builds of the same index key, and the losers of the race now fail instead of serializing. Two concurrent callers for the same NamespacedResource (e.g. a search request and an event handler both missing the cache) both reach bleve.New(dir) for the same file-backed path; bleve errors when an index already exists at that path, so the second caller gets a build error for a perfectly healthy index, where the previous full-function lock guaranteed only one build ran at a time and the second caller got the cached result. The lock was narrowed to protect only the map write, silently changing the concurrency contract of BuildIndex.

[ADVISORY] The new postgres skip ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.') disables CI coverage for exactly the lifecycle path this PR changes, instead of fixing or root-causing the failure. The instrumentation-server test boots a storage server — the code path whose initialization was just moved from lazy per-request to eager constructor-time Init — and its postgres failure in CI is plausibly caused by this PR's own change (e.g. init now running under a different/earlier context in the test harness); skipping it means the regression signal is discarded and the changed init behavior ships with zero postgres CI verification. Reviewers accepting 'performance optimizations' were not shown that a postgres integration test was being sacrificed.

[ADVISORY] Moving s.Init(ctx) from lazy per-request calls into NewResourceServer converts any transient initialization failure (search index build, watcher setup, DB availability) from a per-request error into a hard process-startup failure. Operators get a service that refuses to boot when the search backend or backing store is briefly unavailable (e.g., during a database failover or when bleve file-index directories are in a bad state), where the previous code would start the server and surface the error on affected requests; a single flaky dependency now takes down the whole storage server instead of degrading one code path.

[BUG] Narrowing cacheMu in BuildIndex to only guard the final cache insertion removes the serialization that previously protected the whole build, so concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource can run simultaneously against the same file-backed directory (bleve.New on an already-created path errors, and any cache read outside the lock races with the b.cache[key] = idx write, which can panic on concurrent map access). Two concurrent index builds for one tenant (e.g., a full rebuild racing an event-driven rebuild) either fail with 'index already exists' from bleve.New on the shared dir, or both construct an index and the loser's open index handle is leaked when the winner overwrites b.cache[key]; under contention the unlocked cache lookup can also trigger a fatal concurrent-map-read panic in the storage server process.

[ADVISORY] The new unconditional `t.Skip` for postgres disables the only CI execution of TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer against postgres, inside the same PR that restructures server initialization lifecycle (Init moved from lazy per-request into NewResourceServer in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go). If the postgres failure in Drone is caused by this PR's init-lifecycle changes (e.g., Init now running at construction time against a real postgres backend in the integration harness), CI goes green while the regression ships; the TODO carries no owner or tracking link, so the skip persists indefinitely and postgres coverage of this path is silently lost. 'Works locally' is asserted but nothing in the diff pins down the CI-only failure mode.

[ADVISORY] BuildIndex's cacheMu critical section is narrowed from the entire build (old code: Lock at function entry, defer Unlock) to only the `b.cache[key] = idx` write, so two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key now both execute bleve.New and the full document build concurrently with no serialization, and no test in the diff exercises concurrent BuildIndex. For file-backed indexes (size > FileThreshold), two concurrent builds for the same key race on `bleve.New(dir, ...)` targeting the same directory — the loser errors or both open competing index handles — and both goroutines then write the cache entry, so one fully built index is dropped from the cache while its bleve handle is never closed (resource leak), and duplicate full-document builds waste the very resources this performance PR targets. Callers that can overlap (event-driven builds in search.go's handleEvent path racing a background/other build for the same NamespacedResource) hit this; nothing in the diff or its tests serializes per-key builds or covers the concurrent case.

[ADVISORY] The new log line `s.log.Info("search index initialized", "duration_secs", end-start, ...)` computes duration from `time.Now().Unix()` seconds (start/end defined earlier in init), so any init completing in under one second logs `duration_secs=0`. Operators using this new log line to assess index build performance see 0 seconds for every small/fast namespace (the common case for mem-only indexes below FileThreshold), making the log useless or misleading for the majority of tenants; the same truncation was already tolerated in the histogram metric, but promoting it to a human-readable 'initialized' log line makes the wrong value a first-class signal.

[ADVISORY] NewResourceServer now runs s.Init(ctx) synchronously at construction and returns the error, converting initialization from a per-request lazy step into a hard startup gate that includes the full search index build. During a rolling deploy, a transient DB or search-backend failure at boot makes every new pod exit immediately (crash-loop) instead of starting and surfacing the failure via the per-request Init error path, stalling the rollout; additionally the synchronous search.init at construction delays readiness for large tenants where index build takes minutes, extending the deploy window. The old code's initErr was effectively sticky, so the failure was already fatal at runtime — the surviving delta is that startup now blocks on index construction and fails before any health endpoint exists to observe it.

[BUG] Reordering search.init before initWatcher creates a window in which resources written after the index build reads them but before the watcher starts are never applied to the index, because searchSupport.handleEvent (the only path that applies post-build writes) does not run until initWatcher succeeds. Any write committed during the (potentially long) initial index build is silently missing from search results with no error, no log, and no retry; users see stale/incomplete search results until each affected resource happens to be written again.

[ADVISORY] NewResourceServer now runs the full Init (including the complete search index build) synchronously under whatever ctx the caller passes, converting a lazy per-request initialization failure into a hard construction failure with no retry. A transient DB error or a canceled/short-lived ctx during construction now prevents the storage server from being created at all (crash-loop on restart) where previously the process could start and serve non-search reads and writes; operators of large instances also see startup blocked for the entire reindex duration.

[ADVISORY] The new 'search index initialized' log reports duration_secs computed from time.Now().Unix() on both ends, so any init completing in under one second is logged as duration_secs=0. Operators using this log line to monitor index-build latency see 0 for all sub-second builds and cannot distinguish a fast init from a metric that failed to record, masking regressions under one second; the same truncation flows into IndexMetrics.IndexCreationTime.

If the watcher is responsible for delivering all post-snapshot writes to keep the index current, this ordering could create a window where writes occur after the index build/snapshot but before the watch loop starts. The diff does not show whether initWatcher/watch uses a resume token/resource version to close that window, so the claimed permanent miss can’t be verified from the provided changes alone, but the concern is directly grounded in the new ordering and the added long-duration index-init logging in search.go.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization from lazy-per-RPC to eager-at-construction: NewResourceServer now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if it fails, while the per-method `s.Init(ctx)` guards were removed (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob). This is a real contract/behavior change: the process can now fail to start if Init fails (e.g., search index init/watcher init). Also, init failures are double-logged: `Init()` logs `"error initializing resource server"` when `s.initErr != nil`, and `NewResourceServer` logs the same message again before returning the error. However, the finding’s claim about “retrying per request” isn’t supported by the diff (Init uses initOnce semantics, so subsequent calls wouldn’t retry anyway), making this more of a breaking-change/operational concern than a definite correctness bug.

Previously the watcher was started before search.init, so events written during the (possibly long) index build were received and applied; after this reorder any write landing in the build-to-watch-start gap is silently missing from search results with no event to correct it. This behavioral reordering is not required by the performance goal and is not traceable to a stated requirement.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reorder initialization in `(*server).Init`: it now runs `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (previously watcher start preceded search init). The finding’s described “missed events between index build and watcher start” race is a plausible consequence of this ordering change, but the diff does not show how `search.init` builds its snapshot nor how `initWatcher` delivers and applies events to the index, so the permanent-staleness claim cannot be verified purely from the provided changes. What is verifiable is that the ordering change introduces a potentially significant correctness/consistency risk that should be justified or guarded against.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new postgres skip ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.') disables CI coverage for the server-startup integration test in the same PR that moves initialization into NewResourceServer, masking a failure this change most likely introduced rather than fixing it. The only integration test in the diff exercising server startup no longer runs against postgres in CI, so a real regression in constructor-time Init (e.g. ctx cancellation or DB-readiness assumptions from calling s.Init(ctx) inside NewResourceServer) ships undetected; developers trusting 'Works locally' lose the safety net exactly on the behavior this PR changed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a postgres-only skip in the integration test `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (`t.Skip("...not working with postgres in Drone...")`), reducing CI coverage for postgres. In the same PR, initialization is moved to constructor-time via `NewResourceServer` calling `s.Init(ctx)` and per-RPC `Init` calls are removed. That combination makes it easier for constructor-time init regressions to slip through CI for postgres, even though the diff does not prove an actual runtime failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Calling s.Init(ctx) inside NewResourceServer converts a per-request lazy failure into a hard construction-time failure: with search configured, startup now blocks on a full index build and any Init error (or caller ctx timeout) prevents the server from being created at all. Operators with large indexes get long blocking startup, and any transient DB error at boot now fails server construction where previously the server came up and requests surfaced Init errors lazily; there is no feature flag or options entry to retain the old lazy behavior, so this cannot be disabled without a code deploy. The change is a behavior/deployment-semantics change riding in a 'performance optimizations' PR without a stated requirement.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly moves initialization from per-request to construction time: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns error on failure, while the previous `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` guards were removed from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob. `Init` includes `s.search.init(ctx)` (index initialization/build) and watcher startup, so server construction can now block on index init and fail to construct on init errors or context cancellation/timeouts. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral/deployment semantics change, but not necessarily a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new 'search index initialized' log line reports duration in whole seconds via time.Now().Unix() subtraction, so any build under one second logs duration_secs=0 and multi-minute builds are also truncated, making the metric misleading for the performance work it was added to support. Anyone using this log line (added specifically in this PR as observability for index-build performance) cannot distinguish sub-second builds from near-zero or compare builds finer than 1s; time.Since(start) or the existing histogram metric would report the real value.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go, init() records start/end using time.Now().Unix() and logs `duration_secs` as `end-start` (whole seconds). This truncates sub-second durations to 0 and loses sub-second precision for longer builds. The finding accurately points out the newly added log line (`s.log.Info("search index initialized", "duration_secs", end-start, ...)`) can be misleading for performance/observability even though it doesn’t break functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Reordering init() before initWatcher() in server.Init opens a lost-events window: the search index is built from a snapshot, and every resource written between that snapshot read and the watcher subscribing afterwards is never indexed, because the previous watcher-first order was what guaranteed those in-flight writes were captured and replayed into the freshly built index. For the duration of the (potentially minutes-long) index build, any create/update/delete committed to the store is silently absent from search results indefinitely — not just during the build — since nothing re-syncs the index afterward; users see stale or missing dashboards/folders in search until a full re-index is triggered.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly reorders initialization in `server.Init`: it now runs `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (previously watcher-first). If `search.init` builds an index from a snapshot and the watcher is the mechanism that streams subsequent `WrittenEvent`s into the index, then starting the watcher after the (potentially long) build could miss events occurring during that window. However, the diff does not show the implementations of `search.init` or `initWatcher`, so it’s not verifiable from this PR alone that missed events are unrecoverable or that there’s no replay/catch-up logic. It’s a concrete, diff-grounded concurrency/ordering risk created by the change, but not a provable defect from the shown code alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the whole-body cacheMu lock from BuildIndex turns the cache insert into an unguarded check-then-insert: two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key both pass the cache check and both execute bleve.New on the same on-disk directory path (size > FileThreshold), where bleve.New fails when the path already exists, or both create duplicate mem-only indexes with last-writer-wins on b.cache. Previously the second caller blocked on cacheMu and received the first caller's fully built index; now one of the two concurrent builders gets an unexpected 'index already exists' error for file-backed namespaces (a failed search-index build that used to be impossible), or an orphaned duplicate in-memory index leaks for memory-backed ones.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function (removed at lines ~85-90) but now only locks around the final `b.cache[key] = idx` assignment. This diff-groundedly allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same `key` to both run the expensive build path concurrently (including `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` when `size > b.opts.FileThreshold`) before either stores into the cache. That can lead to concurrent attempts to create the same on-disk index directory and/or duplicate in-memory indexes with last-writer-wins cache behavior—issues that the previous whole-body lock prevented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] NewResourceServer now runs the full Init — including the potentially long-running search index build — synchronously under the constructor's context, converting what was a per-request lazy-init failure into a hard startup failure and binding init lifetime to whatever context the caller happened to pass to construction. For large deployments the initial index build blocks process startup with no bound visible in this diff, and if the construction context is cancelled or carries a timeout, server creation fails outright where previously the system could start and serve non-search traffic; rolling deploys also see delayed readiness proportional to index size.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if init fails (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), while all the per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls in RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.) were removed. `Init` performs search index initialization via `s.search.init(ctx)` before starting the watcher, which can be long-running and now runs synchronously during construction under the constructor-provided context. This changes lifecycle/availability semantics (startup blocking, context cancellation/timeout affecting creation, init failures becoming hard startup failures), matching the finding. It’s an architectural/operational concern visible in the diff rather than a strictly verifiable correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The reorder changes failure blast radius: because search.init now runs before initWatcher and both are gated on s.initErr == nil, a search-backend-only failure (index build error) now leaves initErr set and skips initWatcher, disabling the watch/update propagation pipeline entirely even though it is independent of search. An outage or misconfiguration of the search backend now degrades the whole resource server's change-propagation (watchers get nothing), where previously a search failure could not prevent the watcher from starting; operators debugging 'clients stop receiving watch events' must trace it back to a search index error.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go` the `Init` order was changed so `s.search.init(ctx)` runs before `s.initWatcher()`, and both are only executed when `s.initErr == nil`. This means a failure during search initialization will set `s.initErr` and prevent `initWatcher()` from ever running, whereas previously the watcher was started first and could run even if search init failed afterward. That is a real, diff-grounded change in failure blast radius/resilience (watch propagation becomes coupled to search init success), but it’s not provably an outright correctness “bug” without broader intent/requirements.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] NewResourceServer now runs s.Init(ctx) eagerly at construction under the constructor's context, converting a first-request lazy init into a hard startup dependency. A transient DB failure (or a cancelled/short-lived constructor ctx) during boot now prevents the server from being constructed at all, where previously the process came up and the first request bore/reported the init error; additionally, the full search index build (which search.go's own comment says 'will block startup and continued execution') now runs synchronously inside NewResourceServer, so large deployments block process startup for the entire index rebuild instead of serving degraded until first request. This is a deployment/lifecycle semantics change, not a performance optimization, and nothing in the PR records that the objective was expanded to include changing startup behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes lifecycle semantics: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (server.go `NewResourceServer`), while all per-request lazy `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from RPC methods (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). Since `Init` includes `s.search.init(ctx)` and `search.go` notes init failures “will block startup and continued execution”, this makes search index initialization (and any other init work like `initWatcher`) a constructor-time, synchronous startup dependency. Whether failing fast on init (vs. deferring to first request) is *incorrect* can’t be proven from the diff alone, but it is a substantial deployment/lifecycle behavior change that warrants explicit intent/justification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Twelve exported RPC methods (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob) silently lose their self-initializing contract: the `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { return nil, err }` guard is stripped from each without any change to their documented behavior. Any caller that constructs a server struct outside NewResourceServer (tests, alternative builders, out-of-tree integrations) and relied on 'call any method and the server initializes itself' now executes against uninitialized backends — e.g. Read/List hit a nil store, Search returns 'search index not configured' — instead of getting the previous init-or-error behavior. The public contract changed with no signature change and no explicit acceptance that the lazy-init guarantee was being removed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `s.Init(ctx)` guard from many RPC methods (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob). Initialization is now performed eagerly in `NewResourceServer` via `err := s.Init(ctx)` before returning. This is a real behavioral/contract change from lazy-init-on-first-call to constructor-time init, and any code in the same package that instantiates the unexported `server` type without `NewResourceServer` could now call methods against an uninitialized instance. However, the diff also shows the intended new pattern (always use `NewResourceServer`), so it’s not a clearly verifiable defect for normal consumers; it’s an API/architecture compatibility concern rather than a certain bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Init silently reorders search.init to run before initWatcher, so there is now a window after the index snapshot is built during which the watcher is not running and incoming writes are not observed. A write that lands between the completion of search.init's full index build and initWatcher starting is never delivered to handleEvent; that resource remains absent/stale in search results until some later write to the same resource happens — for a quiescent resource, indefinitely. Under the previous ordering (watcher first, then index build) a write during the build triggered getOrCreateIndex/build and was folded in, so this stale-index window is a new failure mode introduced by an unexplained reorder inside a PR titled 'Performance Optimizations'.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly reorders initialization in `(*server).Init`: it now calls `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (see `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`, moved “Start watching for changes” block below “initialize the search index”). If the watcher is responsible for delivering `WrittenEvent`s to the search index (as suggested by `searchSupport.handleEvent`), this creates a real race window where writes occurring after the index snapshot/build completes but before the watcher starts would not be observed and therefore not indexed until a later event occurs. The prior ordering (watcher first, then index init) did not have this specific gap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the function-wide cacheMu lock from BuildIndex allows concurrent builds of the same index key, and the losers of the race now fail instead of serializing. Two concurrent callers for the same NamespacedResource (e.g. a search request and an event handler both missing the cache) both reach bleve.New(dir) for the same file-backed path; bleve errors when an index already exists at that path, so the second caller gets a build error for a perfectly healthy index, where the previous full-function lock guaranteed only one build ran at a time and the second caller got the cached result. The lock was narrowed to protect only the map write, silently changing the concurrency contract of BuildIndex.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go` the function-wide `b.cacheMu` lock in `BuildIndex` was removed (previously `Lock`/`Unlock` wrapped the entire build) and is now only taken around `b.cache[key] = idx`. With no shown synchronization around the cache read/build path, concurrent callers can both miss the cache and concurrently execute the build, including `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` for the same `dir := filepath.Join(... key.Namespace ... key.Resource ... key.Group)`. This can lead to nondeterministic failures/races during file-backed index creation and differs from the prior serialized behavior guaranteed by the full-function lock.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new postgres skip ('test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.') disables CI coverage for exactly the lifecycle path this PR changes, instead of fixing or root-causing the failure. The instrumentation-server test boots a storage server — the code path whose initialization was just moved from lazy per-request to eager constructor-time Init — and its postgres failure in CI is plausibly caused by this PR's own change (e.g. init now running under a different/earlier context in the test harness); skipping it means the regression signal is discarded and the changed init behavior ships with zero postgres CI verification. Reviewers accepting 'performance optimizations' were not shown that a postgres integration test was being sacrificed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a new skip for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` with the message "test not working with postgres in Drone". In the same PR, resource-server initialization is moved from lazy per-request calls (`s.Init(ctx)` removed from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.) to eager constructor-time initialization (`NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns error if it fails). Skipping postgres in an integration test that may exercise server startup reduces CI verification specifically around the init path this PR changes; this is a concrete, diff-grounded test/coverage concern, not necessarily a functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Moving s.Init(ctx) from lazy per-request calls into NewResourceServer converts any transient initialization failure (search index build, watcher setup, DB availability) from a per-request error into a hard process-startup failure. Operators get a service that refuses to boot when the search backend or backing store is briefly unavailable (e.g., during a database failover or when bleve file-index directories are in a bad state), where the previous code would start the server and surface the error on affected requests; a single flaky dependency now takes down the whole storage server instead of degrading one code path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization semantics: NewResourceServer now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if it fails (`return nil, err`), while many RPC handlers removed their prior lazy `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` checks (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob). This means init failures (e.g., `s.search.init(ctx)` or `s.initWatcher()` inside `Init`) will now prevent server construction/startup rather than being surfaced on individual requests, matching the finding's operational concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Narrowing cacheMu in BuildIndex to only guard the final cache insertion removes the serialization that previously protected the whole build, so concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource can run simultaneously against the same file-backed directory (bleve.New on an already-created path errors, and any cache read outside the lock races with the b.cache[key] = idx write, which can panic on concurrent map access). Two concurrent index builds for one tenant (e.g., a full rebuild racing an event-driven rebuild) either fail with 'index already exists' from bleve.New on the shared dir, or both construct an index and the loser's open index handle is leaked when the winner overwrites b.cache[key]; under contention the unlocked cache lookup can also trigger a fatal concurrent-map-read panic in the storage server process.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire build (lock removed at the top of the function) and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This diff-groundedly removes serialization of the expensive/index-creating portion, so concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same `key` can run `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` against the same file-backed `dir` at the same time. That can lead to conflicting creation/open of the same on-disk index and duplicate work; the previous lock clearly prevented such concurrent builds. The finding's additional claims about concurrent map read panics cannot be verified from this diff alone (no cache reads shown), but the loss of build serialization itself is a real concurrency/correctness risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new unconditional `t.Skip` for postgres disables the only CI execution of TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer against postgres, inside the same PR that restructures server initialization lifecycle (Init moved from lazy per-request into NewResourceServer in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go). If the postgres failure in Drone is caused by this PR's init-lifecycle changes (e.g., Init now running at construction time against a real postgres backend in the integration harness), CI goes green while the regression ships; the TODO carries no owner or tracking link, so the skip persists indefinitely and postgres coverage of this path is silently lost. 'Works locally' is asserted but nothing in the diff pins down the CI-only failure mode.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds an unconditional `t.Skip` when `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer`, with only a TODO comment and no tracking reference. This permanently disables running that integration test for postgres in any environment. In the same PR, `Init` is moved from being called lazily in each request handler to being called eagerly in `NewResourceServer` (`err := s.Init(ctx)`), so skipping the postgres variant of the test reduces coverage exactly when initialization lifecycle behavior is being changed. While the claim about “only CI execution” and the root cause being CI-only cannot be verified from the diff, the loss of postgres coverage due to the new skip is directly shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] BuildIndex's cacheMu critical section is narrowed from the entire build (old code: Lock at function entry, defer Unlock) to only the `b.cache[key] = idx` write, so two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key now both execute bleve.New and the full document build concurrently with no serialization, and no test in the diff exercises concurrent BuildIndex. For file-backed indexes (size > FileThreshold), two concurrent builds for the same key race on `bleve.New(dir, ...)` targeting the same directory — the loser errors or both open competing index handles — and both goroutines then write the cache entry, so one fully built index is dropped from the cache while its bleve handle is never closed (resource leak), and duplicate full-document builds waste the very resources this performance PR targets. Callers that can overlap (event-driven builds in search.go's handleEvent path racing a background/other build for the same NamespacedResource) hit this; nothing in the diff or its tests serializes per-key builds or covers the concurrent case.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex no longer holds b.cacheMu for the whole build; it now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This change clearly allows two goroutines to concurrently run the expensive `bleve.New(dir, ...)` + document build for the same `key` (including targeting the same on-disk `dir` when `size > FileThreshold`) before one overwrites the cache entry. The diff does not show any added per-key serialization or tests covering concurrent BuildIndex, but whether same-key concurrency actually occurs from callers is not directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new log line `s.log.Info("search index initialized", "duration_secs", end-start, ...)` computes duration from `time.Now().Unix()` seconds (start/end defined earlier in init), so any init completing in under one second logs `duration_secs=0`. Operators using this new log line to assess index build performance see 0 seconds for every small/fast namespace (the common case for mem-only indexes below FileThreshold), making the log useless or misleading for the majority of tenants; the same truncation was already tolerated in the histogram metric, but promoting it to a human-readable 'initialized' log line makes the wrong value a first-class signal.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go, init() sets start := time.Now().Unix() and end := time.Now().Unix(), then logs "duration_secs" as end-start. Because Unix() is second-resolution, any initialization finishing within the same second will log 0, making the new human-facing "search index initialized" log line potentially misleading for fast inits (e.g., mem-only index paths). This is an observability/diagnostics quality issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] NewResourceServer now runs s.Init(ctx) synchronously at construction and returns the error, converting initialization from a per-request lazy step into a hard startup gate that includes the full search index build. During a rolling deploy, a transient DB or search-backend failure at boot makes every new pod exit immediately (crash-loop) instead of starting and surfacing the failure via the per-request Init error path, stalling the rollout; additionally the synchronous search.init at construction delays readiness for large tenants where index build takes minutes, extending the deploy window. The old code's initErr was effectively sticky, so the failure was already fatal at runtime — the surviving delta is that startup now blocks on index construction and fails before any health endpoint exists to observe it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes initialization from lazy/per-request to eager at construction: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns the error (server.go), while all the `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` checks were removed from request handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). `Init` includes `s.search.init(ctx)` (which builds/initializes the search index) before starting the watcher. This makes server creation/startup block on and potentially fail due to init/search backend issues, and can delay readiness if index build is slow. Whether this is desirable is an operational/architecture concern rather than a provable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Reordering search.init before initWatcher creates a window in which resources written after the index build reads them but before the watcher starts are never applied to the index, because searchSupport.handleEvent (the only path that applies post-build writes) does not run until initWatcher succeeds. Any write committed during the (potentially long) initial index build is silently missing from search results with no error, no log, and no retry; users see stale/incomplete search results until each affected resource happens to be written again.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly reorders initialization in `server.Init`: search index initialization (`s.search.init(ctx)`) now happens before starting the watcher (`s.initWatcher()`). This creates a plausible consistency gap where writes occurring during a potentially long index build would not be observed by the watcher until after it starts. However, the diff does not show how `initWatcher()` establishes its starting point (e.g., whether it replays from a resource version/offset that would cover the build window), so the claim that such writes are "never applied" and "silently missing" cannot be strictly verified from the shown changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] NewResourceServer now runs the full Init (including the complete search index build) synchronously under whatever ctx the caller passes, converting a lazy per-request initialization failure into a hard construction failure with no retry. A transient DB error or a canceled/short-lived ctx during construction now prevents the storage server from being created at all (crash-loop on restart) where previously the process could start and serve non-search reads and writes; operators of large instances also see startup blocked for the entire reindex duration.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization from lazy per-request to eager during construction: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if it fails (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), while the previous `s.Init(ctx)` calls in request handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.) were removed. `Init` includes `s.search.init(ctx)` (search index initialization/build) and `initWatcher()`, so this can synchronously block server creation and make transient init failures (or a canceled/short-lived construction ctx) prevent the server from being created at all. Whether this is desired is an architectural/operational concern grounded in the diff, not a strictly provable functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new 'search index initialized' log reports duration_secs computed from time.Now().Unix() on both ends, so any init completing in under one second is logged as duration_secs=0. Operators using this log line to monitor index-build latency see 0 for all sub-second builds and cannot distinguish a fast init from a metric that failed to record, masking regressions under one second; the same truncation flows into IndexMetrics.IndexCreationTime.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go, init() records start and end using time.Now().Unix() (seconds) and logs `duration_secs` as `end-start`, so any init finishing within the same second will log 0. The same second-level truncation is used when observing IndexMetrics.IndexCreationTime (`Observe(float64(end - start))`). This is an observability/metrics precision issue rather than a functional defect, but it can mask sub-second regressions and make the new log line less useful.
